extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants and patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for making and responding to rejections under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (and pre‑AIA first paragraph), covering the written description, enablement (including scope), best mode, means‑plus‑function single‑means issues, and related procedural form‑paragraph use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Statutory Basis (35 U.S.C. 112(a) / pre‑AIA first paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations of 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and the pre‑AIA first paragraph setting forth that the specification must contain a written description of the invention and of the manner and process of making and using it 'in such full, clear, concise, and exact terms as to enable any person skilled in the art ... to make and use the same,' and that it 'shall set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute need not be re‑cited in all office actions; it is required in first actions on the merits and final rejections. Where the statute is not being cited in an action on the merits, use form paragraph 7.103. Form paragraphs 7.30.01 and 7.30.02 are to be used ONLY ONCE in a given Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description requirement (Form ¶ 7.31.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre‑AIA 112, first paragraph, as failing to comply with the written description requirement because the claim contains subject matter which was not described in the specification in such a way as to reasonably convey to one skilled in the art that the inventor(s) had possession of the claimed invention at the time the application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01 or 7.103. In the office action identify (by suitable reference to page and line numbers and/or drawing figures) the subject matter not properly described in the application and provide an explanation of the position. The explanation should include any questions the examiner asked which were not satisfactorily resolved and which raise doubt as to possession of the claimed invention at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement (Form ¶ 7.31.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre‑AIA 112, first paragraph, as failing to comply with the enablement requirement because the claim contains subject matter which was not described in the specification in such a way as to enable one skilled in the art to make and/or use the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01 or 7.103. If the problem is one of claim scope, use form paragraph 7.31.03. In the office action identify the claimed subject matter for which the specification is not enabling and explain why the specification is not enabling, applying the factors set forth in In re Wands, 858 F.2d 731, 737, 8 USPQ2d 1400, 1404 (Fed. Cir. 1998) as appropriate. The explanation should include any outstanding examiner questions that were not satisfactorily resolved and that raise doubt as to enablement. Where an essential component or step is not recited in the claims, use form paragraph 7.33.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of enablement / commensurateness (Form ¶ 7.31.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected because the specification, while being enabling for some identified subject matter, does not reasonably provide enablement for other identified subject matter — i.e., the specification does not enable the invention commensurate in scope with the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01 or 7.103. Use when the scope of the claims is not commensurate with the scope of the enabling disclosure. In the office action identify the claimed subject matter for which the specification is enabling (by reference to specific portions of the specification) and identify the aspects of the claim(s) for which the specification is not enabling. State which portion(s) of the statutory enablement requirement are implicated (make/use/make and use) and explain why the specification is not enabling, applying In re Wands factors and including any unanswered examiner questions that raise doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement (Form ¶ 7.31.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre‑AIA 112, first paragraph, because the best mode contemplated by the inventor(s) has not been disclosed; evidence of concealment of the best mode is based upon identified basis/evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01 or 7.103. In the office action insert the basis for holding that the best mode has been concealed (for example, the quality of the disclosure is so poor as to effectively result in concealment). Use of this form paragraph should be rare. See MPEP §§ 2165–2165.04 for considerations and examples of evidence of concealment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of enablement for a single means (means‑plus‑function) claim (Form ¶ 7.31.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected because the claim purports to invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (pre‑AIA 112 sixth paragraph) but fails to recite a combination of elements as required, so it cannot rely on the specification to provide structure/material/acts to support the claimed function; the claim thus recites a function with no limits and covers every conceivable means while the specification discloses at most those means known to the inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01 or 7.103. Use only when the claim recites a single element and that element is in means‑plus‑function format; this situation should be rare. The disclosure is not commensurate with the scope of the claim when only inventor‑known means are disclosed but the claim covers all conceivable means for the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential subject matter missing from claims (Enablement) (Form ¶ 7.33.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim(s) rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre‑AIA 112, first paragraph, as based on a disclosure which is not enabling because the disclosure does not enable one of ordinary skill in the art to practice the invention without specified material/step/feature that is critical or essential to the practice of the invention but not included in the claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.01 or 7.103. In the office action recite the subject matter omitted from the claims and give the rationale for considering the omitted subject matter critical or essential. The examiner shall cite the statement, argument, date, drawing, or other evidence demonstrating that a particular feature was considered essential by the applicant and is not reflected in the rejected claims. See In re Mayhew, 527 F.2d 1229, 188 USPQ 356 (CCPA 1976).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of In re Wands factors in enablement determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When explaining why a specification is not enabling, examiners should apply the factors set forth in In re Wands (858 F.2d 731) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In re Wands factors are to be applied to support enablement rejections and scope‑of‑enablement rejections; explanations should reference those factors as appropriate and may be supplemented by discussion of predictability of the art, quantity of experimentation, and other enablement considerations per MPEP §§ 2164.01(a), 2164.04, 2164.06, and related sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for form‑paragraph use and office action content
rubrics_metrics.description: Various form paragraphs (e.g., 7.30.01, 7.103, 7.31.01–7.31.05, 7.33.01) must be used in specified sequences and with particular content requirements (e.g., identification of claim numbers, references to pages/lines/figures, insertion of bases and explanations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific procedural notes include: the statutory paragraph is only required in first actions on the merits and final rejections; form paragraphs 7.30.01 and 7.30.02 are to be used only once in an Office action; rejections under the written description/enablement provisions must be preceded by 7.30.01 or 7.103; bracketed placeholders in form paragraphs must be filled appropriately (pluralize 'Claim' if necessary, insert claim numbers, insert basis/evidence in bracketed spots); identify and explain subject matter deficiencies with suitable page/line/figure references; indicate any unanswered examiner questions that led to doubt. Where the problem implicates other MPEP sections (e.g., essential components, means‑plus‑function, best mode), use the corresponding form paragraph (e.g., 7.33.01 for missing essential subject matter).
